AGENDA
  GLENDALE ARTS AND CULTURE COMMISSION
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor
  Glendale, CA 91206
Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the City webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire, iOS and
Android devices using a free app called Cablecast and choosing "Glendale TV" from the menu.
Meetings are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
Call (818) 548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the
meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that
agenda item is discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for
assistance, please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services. All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are
received less than 72 hours prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review
in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 72 hours prior to the scheduled meeting or as soon as
practicable. Please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City
provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak
in their native language.

CITY OF GLENDALE
  ARTS and CULTURE COMMISSION
  Minutes of Regular Meeting

  Thursday, December 19, 2024, at 10:00 a.m.
1. ROLL CALL
  •  The meeting was called to order on December 19, 2024, at 10:01 a.m.
  •  Present: Vice Chair Yank, Commissioners Tufenkian, Zadorian (joined meeting at 10:04 am),
  Kazorian, Chairperson Vidor
  •  Absent: Student Commissioner Ataian
  The Agenda for the December 19, 2024, Regular Meeting was posted on December 16,
  2024, on the Bulletin Board outside City Hall.

2. CONSENT ITEMS (Including Minutes)
  The following are routine and may be acted upon by one motion. Any member of the
  Commission or the audience requesting separate consideration may do so by making such
  request before motion is proposed.
  a. Minutes of the November 21, 2024 Regular Arts and Culture Commission Meeting
  Approved with changes.

  •  Commissioner Tufenkian requested to agendize the 2024 -2025 budget for
  review.

  Moved:  Vice Chair Yank
  Seconded :  Commissioner Tufenkian

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vice Chair Yank, Tufenkian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Zadorian, Ataian
  Abstain:  Commissioners Kazorian

  b. Minutes of the December 12, 2024 Special Arts and Culture Commission Meeting

  Moved:  Commissioner Tufenkian
  Seconded :  Chairperson Vidor

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vice Chair Yank, Tufenkian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioners Zadorian, Ataian
  Abstain:  Commissioners Kazorian

3. INTRODUCTIONS AND PRESENTATIONS
  a. Library, Arts & Culture Events – Presented by Loreto Lopez, Program Coordinator

4. WRITTEN COMMUNICATIONS – None
  1
 5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
  Discussion is limited to Items NOT a Part of this Agenda. Each Speaker is Allowed 5 Minutes.
  Members of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission may Question or Respond to the
  Speaker, but there will be no Debate or Decision. The Matter may be Referred to Staff
  Through the Commission Chair for Investigation and Report.
  Speaker: None

(Ms. Fukutomi-Jones informed the Commission that Agenda 7a. 2024-2025 Work Plan Progress
Updates will be taking out of order due to presentations by library staff.)

7. DISCUSSION ITEMS
  a. 2024-2025 Work Plan Progress Updates (discussed out of order)
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that the following updates are programs from the Work
  Plan that have had recent activity.

  CITY WIDE ARTS
  i.  Mural Ordinance – Update
  • Staff is in the process of finalizing the Mural Ordinance and working with public
  art law consultant, Sarah Odenkirk, hoping to have final draft by the new year.

  PERFORMING ARTS
  i.  2025 Performance Series Application – Now Open
  • The 2025 Performance Series Application is now open. The Library, Arts & Culture
  Department of the City of Glendale - on behalf of the City’s Arts and Culture
  Commission - are accepting proposals from qualified candidates who would like to
  participate in its Performance Series Program which includes the Brand Summer
  Music Series and Jewel City Concert Series.

  ARTS AND CULTURAL EVENTS
  i.  Be the Change: 2024 Dia de los Muertos Event
  • GLAC staff presented on this year’s Dia de los Muertos Event as part of the Be the
  Change: I.D.E.A. (Inclusion. Diversity. Equity. Antiracism.) programming. Staff
  thanked the Commission for their support and looks forward to working with the
  Commission in future years. Commission thanked the staff and gave their
  feedback.

  MARKETING AND COMMUNICATIONS
  i.  The ACE Agency – Quarterly Marketing/PR Report
  • Hanya Bruner, Senior PR and Marketing Specialist and project lead from the
  ACE Agency presented a quarterly update recap which included a report on
  marketing, public relations efforts and highlights for the Getty PST ART Exhibit,
  “Blended Worlds: Experiments In Interplanetary Imagination” collaboration with
  JPL at Brand Library & Art Center. Ms. Bruner briefly spoke of other promotional
  initiatives for 2025. Commission asked questions and gave their feedback.

  2
 6. ACTION ITEMS
  a. City-Wide Public Art: Palmer Park Basketball Court Mural
  1. Motion rescinding the Commission’s September 19, 2024, Motion recommending that
  the City Council authorize the City Manager, or a designee, to enter into an Agreement
  for Commission of Artwork with an artist/artist team to design, fabricate and install a
  public art piece for the Palmer Park Basketball Court Mural in an amount not to exceed
  $30,000 dispersed from the Urban Art Program Fund.
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that the Commission approved a motion for the
  recommendation of the Palmer Park basketball court mural and on November 21st.
  Commissioner Tufenkian and Chairperson Vidor requested to agendize to rescind the
  motion. Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated for the motion that was made on September 19th,
  two art piece proposals were submitted for consideration to City Council:
  1st recommendation: Tanner Goldbeck “Palm Trees” and Alternate: 3B Collective “Unity
  through Play.”
  • The Commission gave their feedback and asked questions.

  That the Arts and Culture Commission hereby rescinds the Commission’s September 19, 2024
  Motion recommending that the City Council authorize the City Manager, or a designee, to enter
  into an Agreement for Commission of Artwork with an artist/artist team to design, fabricate and
  install a public art piece for the Palmer Park Basketball Court Mural in an amount not to
  exceed $30,000 dispersed from the Urban Art Program Fund, as more fully outlined in the
  December 19, 2024 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture
  Administrator.

  Moved:  Chairperson Vidor
  Seconded :  Commissioner Tufenkian

  Ayes:  Commissioner Tufenkian, Chairperson Vidor
  Noes:  Vice Chair Yank, Commissioner Zadorian
  Absent:  Commissioner Ataian
  Abstain:  Commissioners Kazorian

  b. Selection and Appointment of a Commission Member to the Arts and Culture
  Grant Program Committee
  1. Motion appointing one Commission Member to serve a one-year term on the Arts and
  Culture Grant Program Committee.

  •  Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated there was a discussion to create an Arts and Culture Grant
  program committee and appointing one specific member to serve on the Committee.

  That the Arts and Culture Commission Hereby appoints Vice Chair Yank to serve on the Arts
  and Culture Grant Program Committee for a one-year term, as more fully outlined in the
  December 19, 2024 Report by the Library, Arts & Culture’s Principal Arts & Culture
  Administrator.

  Moved:  Vice Chair Yank
  Seconded :  Commissioner Zadorian

  Ayes:  Commissioners Vice Chair Yank, Tufenkian, Zadorian, Chairperson Vidor

  3
   Noes:  None
  Absent:  Commissioner Ataian
  Abstain:  Commissioners Kazorian

7. DISCUSSION ITEMS
  a. 2024-2025 Work Plan Progress Updates (discussed above, out of order)
  b. 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games – Arts and Culture Programming
  • Ms. Fukutomi-Jones stated that on December 12, 2024, the 2028 Olympic and
  Paralympic Games – Arts and Culture Programming Committee met to discuss
  recommendations for the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission’s contributions to the
  2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games and meeting notes were included as EXHIBIT A
  in today’s meeting. Ms. Fukutomi-Jones also gave a brief update from City of L.A. and
  L.A. County who are working in tandem. The Commission discussed recommendations
  on next steps, gave their feedback and asked questions.
  • Public Comment: Steven Meek stated he would be in favor if the Arts and Culture
  Commission formed a sub-committee and took the lead in joining other city
  departments, nonprofits, sister cities, and downtown local businesses, also join Disney,
  and DreamWorks, Brand Library as a co-production.
  • Vice Chair Yank suggested a funding plan to have country hospitality houses in
  Glendale and other programming.
  • Chairperson Vidor recommended working on brand identity and creating a branding
  competition where the public is involved with suggestions on branding possibly a tag
  line and graphic logo and suggested ongoing discussions on the 2028 Olympic and
  Paralympic Games arts and culture programming.

8. COMMISSION/STAFF COMMENTS
  • Commissioner Tufenkian wished everyone a happy and healthy new year.
  • Chairperson Vidor wished everyone an artful next year, and stated she attended the first
  open house for the newly remodeled Children’s space at the Central Library.

9. ADJOURNMENT
  Meeting adjourned at 11:39 am
  Moved: Commissioner Zadorian
  Seconded: Vice Chair Yank

  The next Regular Meeting of the Glendale Arts and Culture Commission is January 16, 2025,
  at 10:00 AM in City Council Chambers – 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor Glendale, CA 91206
